Graduate
PhD Program in Physics
The UMass Physics Department hosts about 90 graduate students in our PhD program, with an average of about 15 students in each incoming class. You'll spend the bulk of your first three semesters completing coursework and working as a teaching assistant during the academic year, while starting to explore research. By semester four, you'll be engaged primarily in research activities, but you'll also be attending seminars and taking the occasional special topics course. We'll encourage you, as well, to make use of the many professional development opportunities available through both the department and the Graduate School's Office of Professional Development.

Grants for Travel and Research
Travel Grants
Graduate students planning to present a paper at a conference may apply for travel funds through the department using the Travel Grant Application Form.
Internal Fellowships and Research Grants
You may be eligible for one or more of these Fellowships and Research Grants offered through the university.
External Fellowships and Grants
Whether you plan to go into industry, government service, or academia, learning to write a grant application is an important part of any scientist's training. Individual faculty members and the Office of Professional Development are here to help; please make use of these resources and apply!
The OPD's Grants and Fellowships Page offers a variety of workshops, seminars, and tools for finding and applying to the right fellowship for both U.S. and international students.
For U.S. students in the early part of their graduate program, the NSF's Graduate Research Fellowship Program is highly recommended!
For U.S. students and permanent residents involved in research aligned with the Department of Energy's Office of Science Research Programs, their Graduate Fellowship Program is also highly recommended.
